title: Automated VPC Remediator + Runbook for Common Private Healthcheck Failures (Terraform-aware)
creator: Samir Patel
description: Goal: Ship a defensible, safe-to-run automated remediator plus an on-call runbook that addresses the most frequent Private (VPC) healthcheck failures. This ticket covers: (1) canonical detection thresholds and alert mappings; (2) an automation state machine that performs idempotent corrective actions; (3) tight Terraform/IaC repair hooks to fix drift without risking destructive changes; (4) canary and rollout gating for upgrades that touch private nodes; and (5) clear rollback and escalation paths for oncall.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook documented and linked from oncall rotation page
Automated remediator deployed to staging and evaluated against synthetic failure scenarios
Terraform repair module (vpc-drift-fixer) implemented with non-destructive operations behind a gate
Alert noise reduced by >=40% for top-5 healthcheck failure signatures in staging
Security review completed and KMS access pattern approved
runbook_steps: 1) Triage: Identify failing probe(s) via Grafana dashboard - note probe id and node group
2) Quick checks (2-5 min): verify control plane connectivity, route tables, SG rules, and node disk pressure. Document commands and dashboards to run
3) Soft remediations (automated): trigger remediator 'soft-fix' (service restart, agent restart, refresh config) via API and wait 60s
4) Terraform repair (automated, gated): run vpc-drift-fixer plan -> operator reviews -> apply with lock; forced only if plan contains non-destructive changes
5) Replace node (manual fallback): cordon + drain node -> replace via private autoscaling workflow -> verify healthchecks
6) Rollback for upgrades: if >30% nodes fail post-upgrade within 10m of deployment, initiate automatic rollback to previous image and notify oncall
7) Escalation: if automated fixes fail after 3 attempts or customer-affecting traffic is degraded, page infra-sre and product-ops
8) Post-incident: attach incident artifact (logs, plan outputs, PRs) and file an RCA link in the ticket
automation_design: State machine modes: DETECT -> SOFT_FIX -> TF_CHECK -> TF_APPLY_GATE -> NODE_REPLACE -> ESCALATE
Idempotency: every automation action stores a run-id and checks prior state before mutating infra
Safety gates: TF_APPLY_GATE requires operator approval via Slack approver bot unless run in non-prod
Drift-fixer constraints: never delete resources; if deletion is required, convert to manual remediation step
Rate limiting: remediator will not act on >5 simultaneous nodes for same customer to avoid blast radius
Auditability: all actions produce signed run artifacts stored in S3; KMS-encrypted and accessible to audit/logging team
terraform_plan_policy: Use designated vpc-drift-fixer module (infra/modules/vpc-drift-fixer) with explicit allowlist for fields we mutate
Plan must be uploaded to the ticket as a file and include a deterministic diff summary
Applies in production require two approvals: infra-owner + customer-success if customer-impacting
Apply is executed by automation using ephemeral credentials with least privilege
test_plan: Synthetic failure suite: simulate 6 common signatures (sg-misconfig, route-blackhole, node-disk-pressure, kubelet-crashloop, kube-proxy-misconfig, healthcheck-port-blocked)
Run remediator in staging and confirm each signature resolved within SLA (5 minutes for soft fix, 20 minutes for TF repair)
Chaos test: fire 3 concurrent failures and observe rate-limiting/queueing behavior
Upgrade gating test: deploy minor image canary (5% nodes) and intentionally inject failing probe to validate rollback
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: aggressive automated fixes reduce MTTD/MTTR but increase risk of cascading changes. Mitigation: conservative default mode (soft-fix only) and operator-approved TF fixes.
Tradeoff: blocking TF deletes avoids destructive automation but requires some manual steps and longer toil for operators.
We prefer read-only checks before any change; if plan contains >3 resource modifications, turn into manual review
This ticket focuses on common failures; rarer failure modes should be captured as follow-ups with reproduction artifacts
